Accepted 2026-04-03 initiative-portfolio decision resolved as option B (no moratorium). Operator note confirmed continued initiative growth is expected while swarm-manager matures and inbound brainstorming backlog is imported. No enforcement action is required; the current portfolio posture (47 active initiatives on 2026-04-22, driving toward revenue/quality/meta-opt themes) is already consistent with the selected option. Recording this marker so the decision is not reapplied in future heartbeats.

First vision walk surfaced a coherent lifestyle-bundle vision not previously documented in swarm-manager. Core architectural insight: inventory is the substrate that makes natural product suggestion work (without it, recommendations collapse to ads; with it, they become completion of a known need). Four new initiatives created: routines-app (authority-layer content for cleaning/inspection/maintenance/repair; closes the loop on physical chores), inventory-app (first-class substrate), contact-book-plus (revival of archived contact-book scenario), lifestyle-demand-validation (physical-guide market test runs parallel to routines-app engineering). Full vision frozen into each initiative's orchestration-summary.md. Type-B user framing, routines-as-resource-not-app principle, flexibility ladder (markdown -> list -> light DAG -> rich graph; BPMN 2.0 spec explicitly rejected), and long-horizon robot-orchestration arc are all preserved there. Monetization docs restructured to make consumer-products and affiliate-commerce first-class parallel revenue lines to subscription and services; both carry a mandatory recommendation-blindness architectural rule (agent producing a recommendation must not know what Vrooli sells or earns commission on — offer insertion is post-processing only).

Durable architectural principles landed in the 2026-04-23 walk (reference for future walks and agents): (1) Revenue optimization is a post-processing step, never an input to the recommendation layer. Applies to consumer-products and affiliate-commerce equally; codified in docs/monetization/revenue-lines/. (2) Inventory is the gating substrate for lifestyle-bundle consumer-product / affiliate activation — no scenario activates those revenue lines without inventory-aware state. (3) Routines are infrastructure, not a user-facing build-your-own-workflow product (the original Vrooli died partly from that trap). (4) Flexibility ladder for routines: markdown -> structured list -> light DAG -> rich graph; BPMN 2.0 as a spec is rejected. Vrooli-native rich graph carries the concepts (events / gateways / compensation / interrupt boundaries) without the spec weight. (5) Library and executor are distinct UX surfaces in the routines-app. (6) Prompt-manager distinction: team.enabled=true AND member heartbeats disabled is dormant not quiet. (7) Skills and docs must always invoke scenario CLIs, never raw API calls — if CLI lacks a command, add the command, do not work around. All seven belong in scenario READMEs and docs where applicable.

First calibration walk. Friction surfaced (each is a backlog item or fix): (1) Prep deliverable missing decision option keys — walker had to read decision docs separately to know A/B/C labels. (2) Prep conflates dormant teams (HBs disabled) with quiet teams (HBs active, nothing raised) — led to misdiagnosis of monetization and meta-optimization as active-but-quiet when all 5 + 6 member heartbeats were off. (3) Portfolio-manager is blind to in-flight platform work on branches — retrospective under-counted on a day with ~30 uncommitted swarm-manager files. Acceptable until Git Control Tower ships. (4) Skill referenced prompt-manager team decision-accept — CLI does not expose it; had to go to API PATCH directly. Root cause is a general CLI parity gap; filed as priority-5 backlog item. (5) Web Console TTS pronounces decision IDs inside code ticks as giant cardinal numbers (one quadrillion-plus); filed as TTS preprocessor fix. (6) Accepting a 'add edges' decision does not actually add the edges — only closes the governance step; manual edit follow-up required. Reasonable but non-obvious. (7) Decision phases + chore-audit + ideation ran long; future walks should cap decisions and reach the creative half faster. Positives: prep deliverable structure is strong — synthesized correctly, phase-by-phase; triage/creative split feels right; operator explicitly flagging dual-mode (do the walk + critique the walk) made friction surfacing much better. Operator confirmed morning-vision-walk does NOT need a permanent calibration mode — a few more walks converge steady state, then friction reports stop being novel.
